questions.question:
Six letters S, T, M, P, R and C are written on different faces of a dice. Two positions of this dice are shown in the figures below. Find the letter on the face opposite to M.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3125ab76ffb40776318cccf7cec21f918d7f2846e2c86eebb4a5b9257add676a.png]
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

From the given two different cubes the adjacent sides are as shown below :

As T is common on both the dices, it is clear that S, M, P, and R are adjacent to it, and the remaining i.e. C will be opposite to it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f532d845aa279f30ed0470e0c589ecc05f83513216426f7ad7c3bbf743aebb27.png] 

Opposite pairs:

M → R

S → P

T → C

So, the opposite side of "M" will be side "R".

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question:
‘Blossom’ is related to ‘Wither’ in the same way as ‘Stagnate’ is related to ‘________’.

(The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of

letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic:** Opposites**.

Here,

Blossom : Wither → **Blossom** is the opposite of **Wither**.

Similarly,

Stagnate : Flow → **Stagnate** is the opposite of **Flow**.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements: Some boxes are cartons. All cartons are papers. Some cartons are utensils.

Conclusion (I): No box is a utensil.

Conclusion (II): Some papers are utensils.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f80cd5cf5a196cc435e670786c0e6ad5617b2b1efba78f302c2fce88aae5693.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No box is a utensil → Does not follow (As some boxes are cartons, all cartons are papers and some cartons are utensils. As no direct relation is given between boxes and utensils, therefore it is false.)

II. Some papers are utensils → **F**ollow (As all cartons are papers and some cartons are utensils. As whole cartons comes in papers and has some part common with utensils, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion (II) follows.

Hence, "Option 3" is the correct answer.
